rawFindings.title: Nested arrow functions now miss spacing reports on the outer arrow
rawFindings.explanation: The new token scan walks forward from the first token of the arrow function and stops at the first `=>` it sees. For a nested expression like `(a = ()=>0)=>1`, the outer `ArrowFunctionExpression` will now capture the inner arrow as `arrow`, so the outer `=>` is never checked. This leaves the outer arrow spacing unreported and unfixed.
rawFindings.suggestion: Locate the arrow token that belongs to the current node, e.g. by starting from `node.body` and scanning backward from it, or by constraining the forward scan to the current node's range.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: With input `(a = ()=>0)=>1`, linting only reports the inner arrow, leaving the outer `=>` without the required spaces and producing no fix for it.
